# True or false: Platform

Kubernetes, golden paths, developer platforms, cloud cost and carbon. The simplest option that meets the need wins more often than people expect.

10 statements (Foundation 2, Standard 6, Assured 2). Decide whether each one is true or false before you open the answer. Every answer says why and links to the page that teaches it.

Prefer the terminal? From the repository root, run `python3 exercises/quiz.py --area platform`.

### 1. Kubernetes is the right default for one small team running three services.

Level: Foundation

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**False.** Kubernetes brings real operating work: upgrades, security, networking and skills. For a small team, a PaaS or managed containers meet the need with far less effort. Choose Kubernetes when you need its control or must run the same way on-premises or air-gapped.

Read more: [playbook/platform/cloud-native.md](../../playbook/platform/cloud-native.md)

</details>

### 2. Installing a service mesh early saves effort later, even before you need one.

Level: Standard

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**False.** A service mesh adds moving parts that someone has to run, upgrade and debug. Add it only when a measured need exists and someone owns it. The same rule applies to multiple clusters and multiple regions.

Read more: [playbook/platform/cloud-native.md](../../playbook/platform/cloud-native.md)

</details>

### 3. An organisation with 15 engineers is usually better served by managed services and a good template than by its own developer platform.

Level: Standard

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**True.** With one or two teams, a platform team costs more than it saves. Start one when 3 or more teams repeat the same infrastructure work, or at about 40 engineers. Air-gapped organisations may need one earlier, because they cannot buy managed services.

Read more: [playbook/platform/developer-platform.md](../../playbook/platform/developer-platform.md)

</details>

### 4. A golden path should be optional, not mandatory.

Level: Standard

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**True.** A mandatory path that is slow makes teams route around it in secret. Make it the easiest route, not the only one, and measure time to first deploy. Teams that leave the path own the extra work and write down why.

Read more: [playbook/platform/golden-paths.md](../../playbook/platform/golden-paths.md)

</details>

### 5. Building a developer portal is a good first step for a new platform team.

Level: Standard

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**False.** A portal on top of manual steps is a slower ticket form. Build the self-service capabilities first: provisioning, pipelines, observability and secrets. Add a portal when there is something behind it.

Read more: [playbook/platform/developer-platform.md](../../playbook/platform/developer-platform.md)

</details>

### 6. The same container image should run in every environment, with configuration coming from the environment.

Level: Foundation

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**True.** This is one of the Twelve-Factor principles. An image built per environment means production runs something you did not test. Build one image and inject configuration when it starts.

Read more: [playbook/platform/cloud-native.md](../../playbook/platform/cloud-native.md)

</details>

### 7. Removing idle and oversized cloud resources should come before buying reserved capacity or savings commitments.

Level: Standard

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**True.** Committing before rightsizing locks in waste for one to three years. Rightsize first, then commit only to the stable baseline. Make cost visible to the teams that create it so the savings last.

Read more: [playbook/platform/finops.md](../../playbook/platform/finops.md)

</details>

### 8. A rising cloud bill can be a good sign if the cost per unit of business value is falling.

Level: Standard

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**True.** When the business grows, total spend often rises too. Cost per order, per customer or per transaction shows whether you are getting more efficient. Track unit cost, not only the total.

Read more: [playbook/platform/finops.md](../../playbook/platform/finops.md)

</details>

### 9. Buying carbon offsets lowers a service's Software Carbon Intensity (SCI) score.

Level: Assured

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**False.** SCI, published as ISO/IEC 21031:2024, is a rate per unit of work. Offsets and renewable energy certificates do not change it. Only using less energy, cleaner energy or less hardware lowers the score.

Read more: [playbook/platform/green-software.md](../../playbook/platform/green-software.md)

</details>

### 10. An air-gapped site can use a lighter engineering process, because attackers cannot reach it from the internet.

Level: Assured

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**False.** Code, packages and people still cross the gap, so supply chain and insider risks remain. Run the same practices with different tools: code review, signed builds, scanned dependencies and tested restores. Build once, sign once and transfer the signed artifact.

Read more: [playbook/platform/cloud-on-prem-air-gapped.md](../../playbook/platform/cloud-on-prem-air-gapped.md)

</details>
